title: Evaluator start fails with 503 when its first-brief durable acknowledgement times out queued for the writer (back-to-back evaluation requests)
outcome: Requesting several acceptance evaluations back-to-back does not make an evaluator fail to start because its first-brief durable acknowledgement misses a writer-queue deadline. Either the acknowledgement is reliably durable under ordinary load, or the request waits or queues correctly instead of retiring the delegation.
acceptance: The cause of 'its first-brief durable acknowledgement failed (evaluation submission persistence is unconfirmed (Deadline: queued for the writer))' is diagnosed from host evidence, the writer-tick and phase diagnostics at the failure time, and recorded in a note. It distinguishes writer queue latency, lock contention and memory pressure.

A fix or bound lands: under a test that issues at least 4 evaluation requests back-to-back while the writer is loaded, every evaluator either starts or the request returns a retry-safe outcome whose retry is idempotent. No evaluation is silently lost or duplicated.
The full gate passes on the landed tree, with the review pair clean.
